name: SQL and AI Training Data Pipelines
title: SQL and AI Training Data Pipelines
answer: SQL and AI training data pipelines cover the work of turning rows held in operational databases into datasets that a training or fine tuning job can read. The pipeline usually extracts records from source systems, cleans and joins them with SQL, and writes the result to a store the training job can access. Because the queries define what the model sees, an error in a join or a filter becomes an error in the model, and it is often harder to find there than in the database.

sections.body: SQL and AI training data pipelines cover the work of turning rows held in operational databases into datasets that a training or fine tuning job can read. The pipeline usually extracts records from source systems, cleans and joins them with SQL, and writes the result to a store the training job can access. Because the queries define what the model sees, an error in a join or a filter becomes an error in the model, and it is often harder to find there than in the database.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The pipeline runs on the database engine that holds the source data, on a separate analytical warehouse, or on a distributed query engine that reads files in object storage. Orchestration tools schedule the extract and transform steps, and a storage layer holds the finished dataset, commonly as Parquet or another columnar format that training frameworks read in batches. Compute for the training job itself is usually separate from the compute that runs the queries, so the two sides meet at a shared file or table rather than in one system.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work starts with a question about what the model should learn, which is then written as SQL: select the relevant rows, join the tables that carry the labels, filter out records that are incomplete or out of scope, and shape the columns into features. Teams version the queries alongside the code, run them on a schedule or on demand, and compare the output against expectations such as row counts, null rates and value ranges. Sampling, deduplication and train, validation and test splits are handled in the same pipeline, often with a fixed seed so a rerun produces the same split.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The rights to use each row, the consent under which it was collected and the retention rules that apply to it all travel with the data into the training set, so the pipeline is where those constraints are enforced or lost. Provenance matters in both directions: teams need to know which query produced a given training file, and which training files a given source row ended up in, which is why lineage records and immutable snapshots are common. Access controls on the source tables, masking of personal fields and documented purpose for each dataset are the usual controls, and they are checked by the same review that covers the model.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: More of this work is moving toward treating the training set as a managed data product with its own tests, owners and release notes, rather than as a one off export. Query engines that read object storage directly and tools that track lineage across SQL and training code are reducing the gap between the two sides. The open questions are how to keep a dataset reproducible when the source tables keep changing, and how to show, years later, exactly which rows trained which model.
